barriers.description: User testing was limited to a very small sample of survivors (n=4), restricting the breadth of end-user input available to the design team.
barriers.justification: This constrained designers' ability to facilitate user involvement and evaluate designs with a representative set of users, limiting management of user understanding and iterative refinement based on diverse feedback.
barriers.reference_excerpt: First, user testing was performed by only 4 survivors of breast cancer. However, the original StressProffen intervention was developed with user input, enabling user testing of primarily new exercises in the 2 new versions.

barriers.description: Only newly developed content was user-tested; previously tested original content was not re-evaluated within the adapted versions.
barriers.justification: By restricting testing to only new exercises, designers were limited in their ability to evaluate the full adapted interventions and to manage comprehensive user understanding of the complete program and context of use.
barriers.reference_excerpt: As the original StressProffen content has already been user tested by survivors of cancer as well as health care providers [22], only new, developed content was user tested in the 2 new versions.

barriers.description: Pandemic restrictions forced several workshops to be conducted digitally, which may have affected the development process and team interactions.
barriers.justification: Remote workshops could impede coordination of the multidisciplinary team and the ease of iterative content development and feedback integration, hindering collaboration and shared decision-making workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Third, some of the adaption and development of program content were conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic, meaning that several workshops had to be conducted digitally due to pandemic restrictions. This could potentially have impacted the development process.

barriers.description: The mindfulness-based (MBI) version ended up with more text, more steps, and longer audio than the CBT (CBI) version, making exact equivalence between versions difficult to achieve.
barriers.justification: This methodological/content constraint limited designers' ability to specify identical user requirements and to fully control non-theoretical confounds, affecting workloads for specifying requirements and addressing the holistic experience across versions.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Findings show how this goal was primarily achieved, despite the final MBI-version being slightly longer, with more steps and total words and auditory length compared to the final CBI-version, and the CBI-version having more exercises compared to the MBI-version.
